label: sprites/fw_spit.spr: a sludge spit that splashes, animated

againstClass.words: starts too bright: an attack in its envelope
does not end dark: a decay in its envelope

R1.reason: The brief asks for a sludge spit that splashes. The one frame is a plain, flat, solid disc with a smooth edge. It shows no spit, no droplets, no splash and no sludge. Nothing in it reads as a splash or a spit.

R2.reason: The frame is 32 by 32 and the disc fills most of it, with the border measured at 0, so the size and placement are right. The shape is a perfect circle rather than a splash spreading from a point, so the effect does not fill the frame the way a splash would.

R3.reason: The disc is a neutral pale grey-white with no green. The brief asks for a green-grey sludge, so the colour is wrong for the substance even though the brightness is in range.

R4.reason: The sprite has one frame, but the brief asks for an animated splash, so there is no motion at all. Against the class's measures, the peak is at frame 0 (the class's range is 0.22 to 0.71), the first frame is at full brightness (the class starts at 0 to 0.22), and the last frame is also full brightness (the class ends at 0 to 0.03). It fails on all three counts.

R5.reason: The file reads back as parallel and additive, 32 by 32, one frame, under the name fw_spit. That is a valid GoldSrc sprite, but the class's type and format are not given to the judge, so whether they match the slot cannot be confirmed here.
